Subject: BrightAtlas — Integration & Observability: post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and great context on the search + reranking use case. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can keep momentum.

TL;DR: POC approach, what we'll deliver, and a short list of technical questions we need answers to before the tech sync.

Key integration areas covered
- SDK & auth: recommended approach is Redwood SDK for client apps (auto-instrumentation + safer credential handling) or server-side calls with short-lived OIDC tokens if you need fine-grained access controls.
- Routing & model variants: route high-priority requests to the low-latency tier, background reranks to batch / lower-cost variants.
- Structured output & tool calling: we recommend enforcing a JSON schema for tool responses and using the SDK's structured-output validator to fail-fast on regressions.
- Embeddings & reranker: embeddings for retrieval + cross-encoder reranker for top-k precision, note cost trade-offs.
- Observability hooks: attach a trace id to every request, propagate via header, and expose per-stage latency breakdowns in response headers for dashboards.

Action items (owners & target dates)
1) BrightAtlas: share sample traffic distribution (p95 size, qps, typical seq len) — Priya (by 2026-07-23).
2) Redwood SE: provide an observability field matrix, header names, and a sample SDK snippet — Rishi (by 2026-07-22) (attached).
3) Joint: schedule tech deep-dive for architecture and POC scoping — Camila to propose slots (by EOD 2026-07-21).

Attachments: brightatlas-muthual-action-plan.pdf (MAP), redwood-arch-diagram.png (draft), observability-field-matrix.csv (fields + recommended sampling rates).

Open questions we flagged on the call
- Would you prefer API keys or OIDC flow for server-to-server auth? (we suggested OIDC for short-lived creds)
- Do you have a logging retention requirement (SOC 2/regions) for trace data?
- How aggressively do you want autoscaling to route between low-latency and cost tiers?

Next steps (immediate)
- Priya: send traffic profile and compliance constraints.
- Rishi: technical doc + sample header names (we'll push config you can drop into your gateway).
- Camila & Jonas: follow up with calendar invite for Wed/Thu next-week tech sync.

Thanks —

Hi John / Priya — following up with the technical details we discussed. See inline answers and attached CSV with recommended fields and sampling guidance.

1) Trace propagation / header names - We recommend X-Redwood-Trace-Id (UUID v4) as the canonical trace id header. If you already use X-Bright-Trace we will accept that too; SDK will attempt to read either header.

2) SDK behavior vs gateway proxying - Redwood official SDKs (server-side) will auto-inject trace ids and correlate with our backend traces when you use the SDK client directly. If you terminate requests at your gateway and proxy to Redwood's API, forward the trace header (X-Redwood-Trace-Id) from the incoming request. Our SDKs also provide a small middleware for Express/Go/Java to extract and forward the trace id automatically.

3) Latency breakdown headers - We expose X-Redwood-Latency in the response. Example value: runtime=23;kv_cache=5;network=2 (ms). The header is a semicolon-delimited list of stage=ms pairs so your dashboard can split tokens runtime vs KV/cache vs network. We'll include a ConfigureDashboard JSON snippet in the shared drive.

4) Recommended minimal telemetry fields (non-PII) - trace_id, request_id, model_name, model_version, sequence_length, token_count, latency_ms, cache_hit (true/false), embed_dim, rerank_score. See attached observability-field-matrix.csv for sampling rates by environment.

5) Embeddings & reranker suggestions - For semantic search we recommend the Redwood-embed-1536 model (1536 dim) as a starting point; if you need lower cost we can propose a 768-dim quantized variant with slightly lower recall. Reranker: cross-encoder for top-10 results; we suggest running reranker in a background worker if latency-sensitive queries are routed to a low-latency model.

6) PII & compliance - You can configure SDK to redact PII before logs are emitted (SDK redaction hooks). For SOC 2 retention, we support configurable retention windows per account and can hold trace logs in region-us for 90/180/365-day retention. We'll work with your security team on an export-only retention proof for auditors.

Related links and artifacts
- Observability docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/observability
- Sample dashboard template (Grafana): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/brightatlas-poc/grafana-template.json
- JIRA: INF-482 (POC observability tasks)

Attached: observability-field-matrix.csv (fields + sampling), redwood-arch-diagram.png (draft).

Snippet (Express middleware)

const express = require('express');
const { RedwoodMiddleware } = require('@redwood/instrumentation');
app.use(RedwoodMiddleware.extractAndForward({ header: 'X-Redwood-Trace-Id' }));

This will extract from incoming requests and ensure the header is forwarded to Redwood API calls.

If helpful, I can drop a short demo repo that wires this up end-to-end.
